claims.text: Optimized laser additive manufacturing combined with in-situ V alloying and real-time monitoring will produce a tailored multiphase microstructure in NbTaVW.
The tailored NbTaVW microstructure will enhance mechanical strength relative to conventionally processed MoNbTaW.
The proposed NbTaVW route will reduce irradiation-induced defect sizes relative to conventional MoNbTaW.
The initial NbTaVW alloy has a relatively coarse and poorly controlled microstructure.
A relatively coarse and poorly controlled microstructure is typical of conventionally processed MoNbTaW.
Real-time microstructure monitoring will ensure consistent phase formation.
Real-time microstructure monitoring will ensure a consistent defect distribution.
Substrate preheating above 600 °C followed by rapid cooling will lock in a fine multiphase microstructure.
The proposed processing route will form refined secondary phases and fine precipitates.
The proposed microstructure will contain numerous internal interfaces.
Internal interfaces will impede dislocation motion.
Internal interfaces will trap irradiation-induced defects and impede their propagation.
V addition will reduce helium-bubble size under irradiation.
Controlled solidification kinetics during additive manufacturing will create numerous internal interfaces.
The optimized NbTaVW route will improve yield strength relative to conventional MoNbTaW.
The optimized NbTaVW route will improve fatigue resistance relative to conventional MoNbTaW.
The optimized NbTaVW alloy will maintain high-temperature stability.
The optimized NbTaVW alloy will maintain irradiation stability.

contradictions.description: The material is already identified as NbTaVW, but the intervention is described as in-situ alloying via V addition. The pre-addition composition and amount of additional V are not defined, making it unclear whether V is newly introduced or merely adjusted.
